easy.def: A piece of cloth with colors or a picture on it.
examples: The flag is red, white and blue.
We raise the flag at school.
The flag waves in the wind.

more.def: A piece of cloth with colors and shapes, used as a sign of a country, group or idea.
examples: The flag of our country flies over the school.
The race started when the judge dropped a flag.
Sailors fly a flag from the top of the ship.

easy.def: A special skill or style.
examples: She has a flair for dancing.
A flair for art.
He has a flair.

more.def: A natural talent for doing something well, or a stylish way of doing things.
examples: She has a flair for drawing and can sketch a face in seconds.
He dresses with flair and always wears a bright scarf.
My cousin has a flair for telling funny stories.

easy.def: A thin, small piece of something.
examples: A flake of snow fell on my nose.
The paint came off in flakes.
A flake of ash floated by.

more.def: A small, thin piece of something, such as snow or paint.
examples: A single flake of snow landed on my nose.
Flakes of old paint peeled off the fence.
He brushed a flake of dry skin from his arm.

easy.def: To come off in thin, small pieces.
examples: The old paint flakes off.
The fish flakes.
Dry skin flakes.

more.def: To come off in small, thin pieces.
examples: The old paint flakes off the wall.
The cooked fish flakes easily with a fork.
The dry bark flaked away from the tree.

easy.def: The bright, hot part of a fire.
examples: The candle has a flame.
The flame is hot.
The flame went out.

more.def: The glowing, hot part of a fire that you can see.
examples: The candle flame flickered in the wind.
Flames danced in the fireplace.
The firefighters put out the flames.

easy.def: A tall pink bird with long, thin legs.
examples: A flamingo stood on one leg.
The flamingo is pink.
We saw flamingos at the zoo.

more.def: A tall pink bird with very long, thin legs and a long neck that often stands on one leg in shallow water.
examples: A flamingo stood on one leg in the shallow lake.
The flamingo's pink color comes from the food it eats.
A flock of flamingos waded along the shore.

easy.def: To move up and down quickly.
examples: The bird flaps its wings.
The flag flapped.
The sail flapped.

more.def: To move something such as wings or cloth up and down or from side to side.
examples: The bird flapped its wings and took off.
The flag flapped in the wind.
The sail flapped loudly.

easy.def: A flat piece that hangs loose.
examples: Lift the flap.
The tent has a flap.
The envelope flap is open.

more.def: A flat piece that is fixed at one edge and hangs or folds over.
examples: Lift the flap to see the picture.
The tent door is a flap of cloth.
The flap of the envelope was sticky.

easy.def: A bright light that you use to give a signal.
examples: The boat shot up a flare.
A red flare lit the sky.
The flare showed where they were.

more.def: A very bright light used as a signal, or a sudden bright burst of flame.
examples: The sailors fired a flare so rescuers could find them.
A bright flare lit up the night sky for a moment.
A solar flare is a burst of light from the surface of the sun.

easy.def: To burn with a sudden bright light, or to open out wide.
examples: The match flared and went out.
The fire flared up in the stove.
The cat's nose flared.

more.def: To burn suddenly and brightly for a short time, or to spread out wider at one end.
examples: The campfire flared when he added a dry log.
Her pants flare at the bottom so they swing as she walks.
The horse's nostrils flared as it galloped up the hill.

easy.def: A quick bright light.
examples: I saw a flash of lightning.
The camera made a flash.
A flash lit the sky.

more.def: A sudden, short burst of bright light.
examples: A flash of lightning lit up the sky.
The camera flash made me blink.
A firefly gave a flash and was gone.

easy.def: To shine suddenly and quickly.
examples: The light flashed.
The sign flashed on and off.
Lightning flashes.

more.def: To give off a quick, bright light, or to move very fast.
examples: The lighthouse flashed a warning at sea.
A fish flashed through the water.
The police car flashed its lights.

easy.def: A part of a story that goes back to an earlier time.
examples: The movie had a flashback.
A flashback to her childhood.
He had a flashback.

more.def: A part of a story, a movie or your mind that goes back to something that happened earlier.
examples: The movie used a flashback to show the hero as a child.
The smell of pine gave her a flashback to her grandparents' cabin.
A flashback in the book told how the story began.

easy.def: A small light you hold in your hand.
examples: I use a flashlight at night.
The flashlight is bright.
Turn on the flashlight.

more.def: A small, battery-powered light that you carry in your hand.
examples: We used a flashlight to see in the dark.
The flashlight needs new batteries.
He shone the flashlight under the bed.

easy.def: Bright and showy.
examples: A flashy car.
She wore flashy shoes.
The sign was flashy.

more.def: Bright and showy, in a way that attracts attention.
examples: He drove a flashy red car that everyone noticed.
She wore flashy sneakers with lights in the heels.
The shop had a flashy sign with lots of colored lights.

easy.def: Smooth and even, with no bumps.
examples: The table is flat.
Kansas is very flat.
I lay on the flat rock.

more.def: Smooth and level, with no hills or bumps.
examples: The farmers planted wheat on the flat land.
A flat stone makes a good seat.
The road across the desert is long and flat.

easy.def: Having no air in it.
examples: My bike tire is flat.
The ball went flat.
We had a flat tire.

more.def: Without enough air inside, so that it is not round or firm.
examples: The bike was slow because the back tire was flat.
The flat basketball would not bounce.
Dad fixed the flat tire at the side of the road.

easy.def: To make flat.
examples: I flattened the dough.
Flatten the box.
The wind flattened the grass.

more.def: To make something flat, or to become flat.
examples: I flattened the clay with a rolling pin.
We flattened the cardboard boxes before putting them in the recycling bin.
The strong wind flattened the tall grass.

easy.def: To say nice things to someone to please them.
examples: She flatters the teacher.
I was flattered.
He flattered his friend.

more.def: To praise someone too much, or to say nice things to please them.
examples: He flattered the teacher with kind words to get a good grade.
I was flattered when she said she liked my drawing.
She flatters her friends by telling them they are the best.

easy.def: Making someone look good or feel pleased.
examples: That is a flattering photo.
The hat is flattering.
He said flattering words.

more.def: Making you look or feel good, or praising you in a way that pleases you.
examples: That is a very flattering photo of you.
She wore a flattering blue dress.
He gave a flattering speech about his friend.

easy.def: To show something off to make others jealous.
examples: Do not flaunt your toys.
He flaunted his new bike.
She flaunted her prize.

more.def: To show off something that you have or can do, so that others will notice.
examples: Do not flaunt your new bike in front of kids who do not have one.
The peacock flaunted its beautiful feathers.
She flaunted her new shoes at school.

easy.def: The taste of food.
examples: The flavor is sweet.
I like the flavor.
Vanilla is my favorite flavor.

more.def: The taste of a food or drink.
examples: Vanilla is my favorite flavor of ice cream.
The soup had a rich flavor.
The gum lost its flavor quickly.

easy.def: A small mistake or a bad spot in something.
examples: There is a flaw in the cup.
Mom found a flaw in my plan.
The rug has one flaw.

more.def: A small fault or weak spot that stops something from being perfect.
examples: The jeweler found a tiny flaw in the diamond.
Our plan had a flaw, so we changed it.
A crack is a flaw that can make a bridge weaker over time.

easy.def: A tiny jumping insect that bites animals.
examples: The dog has a flea.
A flea can jump high.
The cat scratched at a flea.

more.def: A tiny insect with no wings that jumps and bites the skin of animals.
examples: The dog scratched at a flea.
A flea can jump far for its size.
Fleas live in the fur of cats and dogs.

easy.def: To run away from something.
examples: The rabbit fled.
The birds flee from the cat.
The people fled the flood.

more.def: To run away quickly from danger.
examples: The rabbit fled from the fox.
The birds fled when the cat crept near.
The villagers fled from the rising flood.

easy.def: A group of ships or vehicles.
examples: A fleet of ships sailed.
The fleet is in the harbor.
The bus fleet is big.

more.def: A group of ships, or vehicles such as buses, that travel or work together.
examples: A fleet of ships sailed into the harbor.
The city owns a fleet of buses.
The taxi company has a fleet of fifty cars.

easy.def: The soft part of your body or an animal's body, under the skin.
examples: The doctor looked at the flesh.
Flesh is soft.
Bones are covered in flesh.

more.def: The soft part of a body between the skin and the bones, or the soft part of a fruit.
examples: A cut went through the skin into the flesh.
The flesh of the peach was soft and sweet.
Bones are covered by muscle and flesh.

easy.def: Able to bend without breaking.
examples: A rubber band is flexible.
The straw is flexible.
A cat's body is flexible.

more.def: Able to bend easily without breaking; or able to change easily.
examples: Gymnasts stretch every day to stay flexible.
The flexible branch bent but did not snap.
Our plans are flexible, so we can go on either day.

easy.def: To hit with a quick movement.
examples: I flick the light switch.
She flicked the crumbs.
He flicked the dust off.

more.def: To move or hit something with a quick, light motion.
examples: I flicked the switch to turn on the light.
She flicked the crumbs off the table.
The cat flicked its tail.

easy.def: A paper that tells about an event.
examples: I got a flier about the show.
The flier is on the door.
We handed out fliers.

more.def: A printed page given out to many people to tell about an event or sale.
examples: I got a flier about the school play.
A flier on the door told about the book sale.
Volunteers handed out fliers about the park cleanup.

easy.def: A person or thing that flies.
examples: The bird is a fast flier.
A frequent flier.
He is a good flier.

more.def: A person, animal or machine that flies.
examples: The falcon is a fast flier.
She is a nervous flier on airplanes.
Bats are the only mammals that are true fliers.

easy.def: A trip by airplane.
examples: Our flight was long.
The flight to Grandma's house was short.
We took an early flight.

more.def: A trip in an airplane.
examples: Our flight left at six in the morning.
The flight to Grandma's house takes two hours.
The flight from Texas to Alaska was long.

easy.def: The act of flying.
examples: The bird's flight was swift.
Wings help flight.
Her flight across the sky was graceful.

more.def: The act or ability to fly through the air.
examples: The eagle's flight carried it over the valley.
Wings make flight possible.
The first flight of the airplane lasted a few seconds.

easy.def: To jump back a little because of fear or pain.
examples: I flinched at the noise.
She did not flinch.
He flinched when the ball came.

more.def: To move back suddenly because of fear, surprise or pain.
examples: I flinched when the balloon popped behind me.
She did not flinch when the doctor gave her the shot.
The dog flinched at the loud thunder.

easy.def: To throw hard.
examples: I fling the ball.
She flung the door open.
He flung his coat.

more.def: To throw something hard in a careless way.
examples: I flung my jacket on the chair.
He flung his bag onto the bed.
He flung a stone into the lake.

easy.def: To turn over quickly.
examples: Flip the pancake.
I flipped the card.
She flipped the page.

more.def: To turn something over quickly, or to toss it into the air so it turns over.
examples: Dad flipped the pancake in the pan.
I flipped the card over to see the picture.
She flipped a coin to decide who went first.

easy.def: To stay on top of water or in the air.
examples: My toy boat can float.
A cloud floats in the sky.
I can float on my back.

more.def: To rest on top of a liquid or drift gently through the air.
examples: A leaf floated slowly down the stream.
The balloon floated up over the rooftops.
Ice floats because it is lighter than water.

easy.def: A group of birds or sheep.
examples: A flock of geese flew by.
The flock is large.
The shepherd watched the flock.

more.def: A group of birds, sheep or goats that stay together.
examples: A flock of geese flew south.
The shepherd watched his flock.
A flock of sheep grazed on the hill.

easy.def: A lot of water that covers dry land.
examples: The flood covered the street.
The river caused a flood.
The flood was high.

more.def: A large amount of water that covers land that is usually dry.
examples: The flood covered the whole street.
Heavy rain caused the river to flood.
The town was cleaned up after the flood.

easy.def: To cover with water.
examples: The river flooded the field.
The pipe flooded the kitchen.
The rain will flood the road.

more.def: To cover dry land with water, or to fill something with too much.
examples: The river flooded the fields.
A burst pipe flooded the basement.
Letters flooded the office.

easy.def: The bottom of a room that you walk on.
examples: The floor is wet.
I sat on the floor.
Toys are on the floor.

more.def: The flat surface at the bottom of a room that people walk on.
examples: She swept the kitchen floor.
The cat curled up on the warm floor.
Wooden floors can be slippery in socks.

easy.def: One level of a building.
examples: Our class is on the second floor.
The elevator stopped at the third floor.
The top floor has the library.

more.def: One level of a building, such as the first, second or third floor.
examples: My aunt lives on the tenth floor of her building.
The art room is on the second floor.
Push the button for the fourth floor.

easy.def: To fall or drop heavily.
examples: I flop on the couch.
The fish flopped.
She flopped into a chair.

more.def: To drop or fall in a loose, heavy way.
examples: I flopped onto the couch after school.
The fish flopped on the deck of the boat.
She flopped into a chair and sighed.

easy.def: Something that does not work well.
examples: The show was a flop.
The plan was a flop.
The game was a flop.

more.def: Something that fails or does not do well.
examples: The new snack was a flop and no one bought it.
The show was a flop because few people came.
The movie was a flop and people left early.

easy.def: A person who sells flowers.
examples: The florist made a bouquet.
We went to the florist.
The florist sold roses.

more.def: A person who sells flowers and arranges them into bouquets and decorations.
examples: The florist tied the roses and tulips together into a pretty bouquet.
We bought flowers for Grandma from the florist on Main Street.
The florist made the table decorations for the wedding.

easy.def: A thin string for cleaning between teeth.
examples: I use floss every night.
The dentist gave me floss.
Floss is thin.

more.def: A thin, strong thread that you pull between your teeth to clean them.
examples: The dentist showed me how to use floss between my teeth.
I use floss every night before I go to bed.
The floss caught a bit of popcorn that was stuck.

easy.def: To clean between your teeth with string.
examples: I floss every night.
He flosses his teeth.
Don't forget to floss.

more.def: To clean between your teeth with a thin thread.
examples: I brush and floss my teeth before bed.
The dentist told us to floss every day.
She flossed carefully around her braces.

easy.def: A soft powder used to make bread and cakes.
examples: We need flour for the cake.
Flour is made from wheat.
I spilled flour on the table.

more.def: A fine powder made by grinding grains such as wheat, used for baking bread, cakes and pasta.
examples: The baker mixed flour, water and yeast to make bread dough.
Wheat is ground into flour at a mill.
Dad dusted the table with flour so the dough would not stick.

easy.def: To move along smoothly, like water.
examples: Water flows in the stream.
The river flows to the sea.
Honey flows slowly.

more.def: To move along smoothly in one direction, as water does.
examples: The stream flows past the old mill.
Water flowed out of the tap.
Cars flowed along the highway.

easy.def: A steady stream of something.
examples: The flow of the river is slow.
There was a flow of water.
A flow of cars passed.

more.def: A steady movement of something, such as water or people.
examples: The flow of the river slowed in summer.
A flow of people left the stadium.
The nurse watched the flow of water into the cup.

easy.def: The colorful part of a plant.
examples: The flower smells nice.
Bees visit the flower.
I picked a flower.

more.def: The colorful part of a plant that makes seeds, often with petals.
examples: A bee landed on the yellow flower.
The garden is full of flowers.
She picked a flower for her teacher.

easy.def: A sickness that gives you a fever and makes you ache.
examples: I have the flu.
The flu makes you sick.
She stayed home with the flu.

more.def: An illness that spreads easily and causes fever, aches and coughing.
examples: I stayed home with the flu for a week.
Many kids caught the flu this winter.
A flu shot can help protect you.

easy.def: Soft and light, like fur or a cloud.
examples: The cat is fluffy.
A fluffy cloud.
The towel is fluffy.

more.def: Soft and light, like fur, feathers or a cloud.
examples: The fluffy kitten was soft to hold.
A fluffy white cloud floated across the sky.
We dried off with big fluffy towels.

easy.def: Something that flows, like water.
examples: Water is a fluid.
The fluid is thin.
Drink plenty of fluids.

more.def: A substance such as water or air that can flow.
examples: Water and juice are fluids.
The doctor said to drink plenty of fluids.
A fluid takes the shape of its container.

easy.def: A lucky thing that happens by chance.
examples: It was a fluke.
The win was a fluke.
A lucky fluke.

more.def: Something good that happens by pure luck and not because of skill; also the broad tail fin of a whale.
examples: It was a fluke that I hit the target on my first try.
The win was no fluke; the team had practiced all week.
The whale lifted its fluke above the waves as it dived.

easy.def: To not pass a test or a class.
examples: I hope I do not flunk the test.
He flunked the quiz.
She flunked math last year.

more.def: To fail a test or a class.
examples: I studied hard so I would not flunk the spelling test.
He flunked the quiz because he did not read the chapter.
She was afraid she would flunk her driving test.

easy.def: To clean with a rush of water.
examples: I flush the toilet.
The pipes flushed.
Please flush.

more.def: To clean something out with a strong rush of water.
examples: Please flush the toilet when you finish.
The plumber flushed the pipes with water.
Rain flushed the dirt from the street.

easy.def: To turn red in the face.
examples: Her face flushed.
He flushed with shame.
I flushed with embarrassment.

more.def: To become red in the face, because of feeling hot or embarrassed.
examples: His face flushed when everyone looked at him.
She flushed with embarrassment.
Her cheeks flushed from the cold.

easy.def: A long, thin instrument you blow across.
examples: She plays the flute.
The flute sounds sweet.
I blew into the flute.

more.def: A long, thin musical instrument that you hold sideways and play by blowing across a hole and pressing keys.
examples: She learned to play the flute in the school band.
The flute made a soft, sweet sound.
In the story, the boy played a flute and the mice followed him.

easy.def: To flap quickly and lightly.
examples: The butterfly fluttered.
The flag fluttered.
Her heart fluttered.

more.def: To move or flap quickly and lightly in the air.
examples: The butterfly fluttered from flower to flower.
The flag fluttered in the breeze.
My heart fluttered with excitement.

easy.def: A light, quick flapping movement.
examples: I felt a flutter.
The flutter of wings.
A flutter of leaves.

more.def: A quick, light flapping movement, or a feeling of nervous excitement.
examples: We heard the flutter of wings above us.
I felt a flutter in my stomach before the show.
A flutter of leaves fell from the tree.

easy.def: To move through the air.
examples: Birds fly in the sky.
The plane flies over our house.
My kite flew high.

more.def: To move through the air using wings, or to travel in an aircraft.
examples: Geese fly south in big V-shaped groups each fall.
We flew to Florida to visit my cousins.
The pilot flies a plane across the ocean.

easy.def: A small bug with wings.
examples: A fly landed on my food.
The frog ate a fly.
The fly buzzed by my ear.

more.def: A small insect with two wings that is often found around food and garbage.
examples: A fly buzzed against the window and could not find the way out.
Frogs catch flies with their long, sticky tongues.
Flies can walk upside down on the ceiling.

easy.def: A paper that tells about an event.
examples: I got a flyer about the fair.
The flyer is bright.
They handed out flyers.

more.def: A single printed page that advertises an event or sale.
examples: I got a flyer about the school fair.
The flyer had a picture of a clown.
They handed out flyers in the park.
